newsitem.title: JAPAN: Muto forex comments don't reflect Japan policy-MOF.
newsitem.headline: Muto forex comments don't reflect Japan policy-MOF.

text.p: Comments by cabinet minister Kabun Muto about foreign exchange markets do not reflect Japan's official policy, a Ministry of Finance official told Reuters on Friday.
The MOF official, who declined to be idenified, told Reuters: "Muto's remarks regarding the dollar/yen rate do not reflect the official policy of the Japanese government."
"The official view is, as Finance Minister (Hiroshi Mitsuzuka) said, that the yen's recent falls are overdone and (the ministry) is concerned about it," he added.

Muto, director-general of the Management and Coordination Agency, said earlier that any "artificial" attempt to check a further yen fall could fail in the current environment of a continuing capital outflow from Japan.
He said that there was nothing wrong with the dollar moving above 125 yen, adding that, in terms of purchasing power, 150 yen to the dollar would be an appropriate level.
The ministry official also said Japan would take decisive measures to deal with excessive moves in the currency markets.
The dollar fell slightly on the remarks by the MOF official, hovering around 125.90/05 yen at 0314 GMT.
